title: The sign of a 1982-2022 DOISST feedback adjustment depends on drift and step dates in five linear models
abstract: We tested how gradual product differences change the inferred radiation effect of DOISST input steps. We used verified complete monthly SST and radiation aggregates for five atmosphere-model Green's functions, two reference products and 1982-2022. With five fixed dates and the mean of ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2 as reference, raw-minus-adjusted trend-ratio feedback is +0.057 W m-2 K-1 without drift, -0.076 with linear drift and -0.034 with quadratic drift. Conditional 95% intervals include zero for all three. With only the three reported mean-step dates, the linear result stays positive at +0.009. Four-year local fits retain warm steps of +0.097 K in 2005 and +0.090 K in 2020; their radiation signatures are consistent with uniform warming. An exact scalar contrast shows how smooth SST and radiation difference slopes control the feedback sign. Along the fitted five-date drift path, the mean effect reaches zero at 39% of the fitted drift. Buffered held-out reconstruction favors no drift for SST and the feedback contrast, but smooth terms for mean radiation. Thus the reversed fit is not established as a better correction. The test shows conditional attribution uncertainty, not a new true SST record or observed radiation change. It does not reproduce the source's full spatial correction. Shared observations, fixed dates, two references, linear kernels and missing CCI monthly radiation limit inference. Code, source hashes, figures, all tested cases and an independent QR audit are included.

display.caption: The 1982-2022 feedback effect changes with drift assumptions and the reference in a five-date fit. Left: five-model mean and conditional paired 24-month block intervals. Right: constrained linear drift from zero to the fitted value. These fits do not establish which correction is true. Three-date results are given separately.

Local January 2005 and July 2020 warm steps remain visible. The radiation departure from a uniform-warming response has an interval that includes zero in the four-year fits. Local events do not uniquely set the total feedback adjustment.

DOISST minus the mean of ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2, in SST and mean model radiation. Step-only and joint drift fits can assign different step sizes to the same record. Held-out checks favor the step-only fit for the feedback contrast.
